slots.practicalActivity: Take a vague prompt you've written in the past (or write one now, e.g. 'write something about our product'), rewrite it with an explicit task, format, and constraints, and run both versions through a model to compare the outputs.
slots.deliverable: The original vague prompt, the rewritten prompt, and both outputs side by side.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a zero-shot and a few-shot version of the same classification prompt (e.g. sentiment or support-ticket category) and test both against three different inputs to see where the few-shot examples change the result.
slots.deliverable: The zero-shot prompt, the few-shot prompt with its examples, and the results for all three test inputs under each.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a reusable prompt template with placeholders for a real recurring task, then deliberately trigger two of the chapter's failure modes against it (e.g. an injection attempt and an ambiguous input) and document exactly what went wrong in each case.
slots.deliverable: The template file and two short failure write-ups, each with the triggering input and the broken output.

slots.practicalActivity: Run three deliberate iterations on one prompt from this chapter, logging the exact change made and its effect on the output at each step, instead of changing everything at once.
slots.deliverable: A three-row iteration log: version, change made, resulting output/effect.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a personal 'prompt checklist' reference doc from this chapter's lessons (specificity, examples, system prompt, template structure, common failure modes) and apply it to two prompts you wrote earlier in the chapter, noting what each one was still missing.
slots.deliverable: The prompt checklist doc plus notes on two prompts it caught gaps in.

slots.practicalActivity: Run the guide's crates-of-apples word problem (or a similar multi-step problem) through a model once asking directly for the answer, then again with 'think step by step before answering,' and confirm whether the step-by-step version catches a mistake the direct version made.
slots.deliverable: Both transcripts side by side, with a one-line note on which answer was correct and why.

slots.practicalActivity: Sample the same reasoning prompt three times at a non-zero temperature and take a majority vote across the answers; separately, test a role-based system prompt (e.g. 'You are a senior tax auditor') against the same question with no role assigned, and compare the two responses.
slots.deliverable: The three sampled answers with the majority-vote result, plus the role-based vs. no-role comparison.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a prompt that forces JSON-only output matching a schema you define (e.g. {category, confidence, reason}), run it against three different inputs, and validate that every response actually parses as valid JSON matching the schema.
slots.deliverable: The prompt, the schema, and three parsed JSON outputs confirmed valid.

slots.practicalActivity: Break one complex task (e.g. 'summarize this document, then draft a reply based on the summary') into a two-step prompt chain, feeding step one's real output into step two's prompt as input.
slots.deliverable: Both prompts in the chain, step one's output, and the final step-two output it fed into.

slots.practicalActivity: Combine two techniques from this chapter (e.g. chain-of-thought plus role-based prompting) on one real task and compare the result against the single-technique baseline from earlier in the chapter.
slots.deliverable: The combined-technique prompt and output, set against the earlier single-technique baseline for the same task.

slots.practicalActivity: Take one of your earlier prompts and split it into what's 'prompt' (instructions, format, examples) versus what's 'context' (background facts, retrieved data, history), listing every piece under the correct heading.
slots.deliverable: A two-column breakdown of one real prompt into its prompt-engineering vs. context-engineering pieces.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a real token budget worksheet for a use case of your choosing: reserve tokens for output, account for fixed costs (system prompt, tool descriptions), and cap the variable cost (retrieved documents, history).
slots.deliverable: A completed token budget worksheet with real numbers for each category.

slots.practicalActivity: Take an oversized context blob (a long document or chat history) and compress it to fit your budget worksheet's cap; then reorder the remaining pieces by priority and write one sentence justifying the final order.
slots.deliverable: The original oversized context, the compressed version, and the final prioritized ordering with justification.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a tool schema (name, description, input_schema) for a real tool relevant to your use case, then test whether the description is specific enough by seeing if a model correctly chooses to call it (or not) on three different inputs.
slots.deliverable: The tool schema plus the three test results showing correct or incorrect tool-choice behavior.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a real long-term memory record, in JSON, for a fact worth remembering about a user across sessions, including a confidence score and a saved_at date, and write one sentence describing how you'd detect that fact going stale.
slots.deliverable: The JSON memory record plus the one-sentence staleness-check plan.

slots.practicalActivity: Assemble a complete context package for your eventual capstone use case: a system prompt, the token budget worksheet, the tool descriptions, and at least one long-term memory record, all in one folder.
slots.deliverable: A folder containing the four context artifacts, ready to carry into the capstone.

slots.practicalActivity: Write three eval cases — one common, one edge, one adversarial — for a prompt you've built earlier in the course, each with a real input and a defined expected_behavior, and run the prompt against all three by hand to see whether it actually passes.
slots.deliverable: Three eval cases in the lesson's JSON shape, plus the pass/fail result of running each by hand.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a script that loops over your eval set, calls the model API for each case, and automatically scores each result pass or fail against its expected_behavior.
slots.deliverable: A working script that runs your eval set end to end and prints a pass/fail summary.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a second version of a prompt you've already tested, run both version A and version B through your automated eval script against the same eval set, and compare the two pass rates.
slots.deliverable: Both prompt versions and a side-by-side pass-rate comparison from your automated test script.

slots.practicalActivity: Take a real failure you found earlier in the course, add it as a permanent known-failure case in your eval set, and confirm your current best prompt still passes it — a real regression tripwire, not a hypothetical one.
slots.deliverable: The new regression eval case added to your eval set, plus the passing test-run result for it.

slots.practicalActivity: Grow your eval set to at least 10 real cases covering all four categories (common, edge, known-failure, adversarial) for the use case you'll carry into the capstone, and run the full set through your automated testing script.
slots.deliverable: A 10+ case eval_set.json file and the automated test run's full pass/fail results.

slots.practicalActivity: Pick a real use case for your capstone prompt library and write the project brief: the system prompt's purpose, at least two task-specific templates you'll need, and the deliverables the library must contain.
slots.deliverable: A written capstone brief naming the use case, the required templates, and the deliverables.

lessons.title: Capstone: Building a Prompt Library for a Real Use Case

slots.practicalActivity: Create the real four-folder prompt-library layout (prompts/, context/, evals/, CHANGELOG.md) for your capstone use case, and write system.md plus at least one task-specific template applying a Chapter 2 technique.
slots.deliverable: The populated prompts/ folder (system.md and at least one template) inside the four-folder library structure.

slots.practicalActivity: Write budget.md (your Lesson 13 token-budget worksheet, filled in for real) and tools.json (real tool schemas from Lesson 16) for your capstone prompt library's context/ folder.
slots.deliverable: Completed budget.md and tools.json files inside the library's context/ folder.

slots.practicalActivity: Build eval_set.json with at least 10 real cases across all four categories for your capstone prompt library, run it against your prompts with the automated testing script, and log the first dated entry in CHANGELOG.md with a real pass rate.
slots.deliverable: A populated evals/ folder (eval_set.json and a results/ run) plus a CHANGELOG.md with one real, dated entry.

slots.practicalActivity: Make one deliberate change to your prompt library, run the A/B comparison against your eval set to get a second dated CHANGELOG.md entry, and write a portfolio summary describing the measured pass-rate improvement between the two versions.
slots.deliverable: A second CHANGELOG.md entry with its pass rate, plus a portfolio summary paragraph citing the real before/after numbers.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can write and systematically test production-grade prompts, manage a model's context window budget deliberately, and ship a versioned prompt library with a real eval set and a changelog that proves whether each change actually helped.
